title: Optimal Seeding for Encouragement-Dose Contrasts with Paired Sources
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR — D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field); paper_score_ceiling 5.8 < 7.4. Final math and decision panels pass with no findings.
gap_reasons: The exact optimizer and matched information regimes are proved only for the highly specialized cycle with homogeneous exposure-cell means and either independent errors or the chosen cycle-Laplacian precision model.

Outside the cycle, the note proves only a union-bound obstruction for observing the two-source cell; it supplies neither a matching support probability nor an information or design frontier, so the broader paired-source motivation remains one-sided.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the exact cycle E-optimal assignment frontier, a sparse-budget information comparison, and a one-sided support obstruction for general paired-source incidence. The final math and decision panels passed without findings after the correlated-Gaussian model and theorem positioning were repaired. The field-level novelty gate still rejected the specialized cycle scope; a matching general-graph support and information frontier remains a separate possible extension, not a result of this run.
tldr: In a paired-source encouragement-dose experiment, each focal unit is incident to two candidate seeds and the causal targets are the adjacent intention-to-treat increments from zero to one and from one to two encouraged sources. For the cyclic degree-two incidence design, the paper gives the exact E-optimal fixed-budget assignment, including parity, endpoint, and tie cases. The optimized sparse information is \((1-1/\sqrt2)k/\sigma^2\), whereas cycle complete randomization loses the two-source cell below the \(\sqrt n\) scale, has a Poisson information law at that boundary, and carries only \(k^2/(n\sigma^2)\) information above it. More generally, if \(q_n\) distinct unordered seed pairs are represented, then the two-source support probability is at most \(\min\{1,q_n(k)_2/(n)_2\}\); total focal-unit multiplicity \(m_n\) affects realized cell counts and conditional information but not whether an already represented pair creates the cell. Thus \(q_n=\Theta(n)\) yields the general sub-\(\sqrt n\) barrier, while \(m_n=\Theta(n)\) alone does not locate the support elbow. For the correlation extension, the homogeneous exposure-response mean model is paired with the alternative correlated-Gaussian covariance having precision \(\sigma^{-2}\{I_n+\rho L(C_n)\}\), which replaces the independent-error covariance for that theorem and equals it at \(\rho=0\). For fixed \(\rho\geq0\), the optimized sparse constant becomes \(1+\rho-1/\sqrt2\), while the cycle complete-randomization Poisson and supercritical scales are multiplied by \(1+2\rho\); the support elbow is unchanged. Actual activated-peer reinforcement requires a compliance and exclusion model and is not claimed here.
gap: Existing free-allocation contrast theory, linear-network and CAR design, and graph-cut rerandomization optimize treatment or network-effect contrasts on vertices or take the assignment criterion as given. They do not determine which exact-\(k\) cycle assignments identify all three edge-exposure cells and maximize the minimum information eigenvalue for both adjacent reinforcement increments, and circular-run theory does not attach its count laws to this information criterion.
fill: The paper supplies the exact attainable count geometry, a strict-concavity certificate, the complete integer optimizer including ties and endpoints, and the three-regime sparse information and detection frontier.
